paragraphs: Govstream.ai sells permitting software to cities and counties, aimed at the point where an applicant is trying to work out what their project actually requires. It is positioned as an addition to the systems a city already runs rather than a replacement for them.

A research assistant answers questions about a specific property, using zoning, overlays and GIS data so an applicant can see what applies to that parcel. An application assistant takes the plans first, pulls project details out of them and prefills the forms. A completeness score flags gaps before anything is submitted. Staff get a console that holds permit data, adopted codes, GIS layers, historical permits and conversations in one searchable place.

The company names Bellevue, Washington, as the site of its first pilot and reports that it cut inbound questions. Louisville is described as building an end-to-end workflow meant to stop incomplete applications before they are submitted. Everett is listed as another partner city. The site describes the product as SOC 2-ready and able to work with a city's existing infrastructure. Its press section links coverage of a seed round.
